tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available, or one your own work this turn made available; others are refused, and one that later stops being available is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and other answers), so do not guess. tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

2	"""Software reference model of the recovered FIR, bit-exact to the hardware.
3	
4	Arithmetic (recovered & confirmed against the netlist):
5	  acc   = sum_k  x_int[n-k] * h_int[k]      # int, x/h are int16 (Q1.15)
6	  y_int = (acc + 2**14) >> 15               # round half toward +inf, arithmetic shift
7	  y_int = sat16(y_int)                      # saturate to [-32768, 32767]
8	"""
9	import json
10	
11	def load_coeffs(path="recovered/coeffs.json"):
12	    return json.load(open(path))["coeffs_q15"]
13	
14	def sat16(v):
15	    if v > 32767:  return 32767
16	    if v < -32768: return -32768
17	    return v
18	
19	def fir_filter(x_int, h):
20	    """x_int: list of int16 input samples (no leading flush needed; history is
21	    zero before index 0). Returns list of int16 outputs, same length, aligned so
22	    y[n] corresponds to x[n] (the filter's internal group delay is inherent)."""
23	    N = len(h)
24	    y = []
25	    for n in range(len(x_int)):
26	        acc = 0
27	        for k in range(N):
28	            idx = n - k
29	            xk = x_int[idx] if idx >= 0 else 0
30	            acc += xk * h[k]
31	        y.append(sat16((acc + (1 << 14)) >> 15))
32	    return y
33	
34	if __name__ == "__main__":
35	    import sys, wave
36	    from array import array
37	    h = load_coeffs(sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "recovered/coeffs.json")
38	    w = wave.open(sys.argv[1], "rb")
39	    a = array("h"); a.frombytes(w.readframes(w.getnframes()))
40	    import sys as _s
41	    if _s.byteorder == "big": a.byteswap()
42	    y = fir_filter(list(a), h)
43	    print("filtered %d samples; first 10 out = %s" % (len(y), y[:10]))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""CSAW 2026 Challenge 3 -- Phase 05 DSP characterization.

FACET: coeffs-impulse
Load the recovered Q1.15 FIR taps and characterize the impulse response.

The impulse response of an FIR filter IS its coefficient set: h[n] = coeffs[n].
This script loads the golden taps, measures every structural/gain property the
facet calls for, writes impulse_response.csv, and emits coeffs-impulse.json.

Run:
  python C:/Users/lowbr/Documents/College/AI/CSAW_FIN_worktrees/05d-opus-dsp/experiments/phase05/05d-opus-dsp/ai/analysis/coeffs-impulse.py

All inputs are read from the read-only golden/ artifacts; nothing is modified.
"""
import json
import math
import csv
import os
import sys
import importlib.util

# ---- Absolute paths (do not depend on cwd) ---------------------------------
ROOT = "C:/Users/lowbr/Documents/College/AI/CSAW_FIN_worktrees/05d-opus-dsp/experiments/phase05/05d-opus-dsp"
COEFFS_PATH = os.path.join(ROOT, "golden", "coeffs.json")
SW_FIR_PATH = os.path.join(ROOT, "golden", "sw_fir.py")
OUT_JSON = os.path.join(ROOT, "reports", "analysis", "coeffs-impulse.json")
OUT_CSV = os.path.join(ROOT, "reports", "analysis", "impulse_response.csv")

Q15 = 32768.0  # 2^15, the Q1.15 scale (coeff/Q15 == float gain)


def load_golden_coeffs():
    """Load taps directly from the golden JSON, and cross-check against the
    golden sw_fir.load_coeffs() loader so we are provably using the same data
    path the bit-exact software model uses."""
    with open(COEFFS_PATH) as f:
        meta = json.load(f)
    coeffs = meta["coeffs_q15"]

    # Cross-check via the golden loader (fidelity guarantee).
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("sw_fir_golden", SW_FIR_PATH)
    sw = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(sw)
    coeffs_via_loader = sw.load_coeffs(COEFFS_PATH)
    assert coeffs_via_loader == coeffs, "golden loader disagreement!"

    return coeffs, meta


def classify_linear_phase_type(h):
    """Type I/II/III/IV per the standard linear-phase FIR taxonomy.

    symmetry  x  N parity  -> type
    symmetric  + N odd       Type I
    symmetric  + N even      Type II
    antisym    + N odd       Type III
    antisym    + N even      Type IV
    """
    N = len(h)
    is_sym = all(h[k] == h[N - 1 - k] for k in range(N))
    is_antisym = all(h[k] == -h[N - 1 - k] for k in range(N))
    n_odd = (N % 2 == 1)
    if is_sym and n_odd:
        t = "Type I"
    elif is_sym and not n_odd:
        t = "Type II"
    elif is_antisym and n_odd:
        t = "Type III"
    elif is_antisym and not n_odd:
        t = "Type IV"
    else:
        t = "none (not linear phase)"
    return t, is_sym, is_antisym


def to_db(ratio):
    if ratio == 0:
        return float("-inf")
    return 20.0 * math.log10(abs(ratio))


def main():
    h, meta = load_golden_coeffs()
    N = len(h)

    # ---- Structural symmetry -----------------------------------------------
    ftype, is_symmetric, is_antisymmetric = classify_linear_phase_type(h)

    # Per-element symmetry defects (which taps, if any, break h[k]==h[N-1-k]).
    asymmetry_defects = [
        {"k": k, "h_k": h[k], "h_mirror": h[N - 1 - k], "diff": h[k] - h[N - 1 - k]}
        for k in range(N // 2)
        if h[k] != h[N - 1 - k]
    ]
    max_abs_asymmetry = max((abs(d["diff"]) for d in asymmetry_defects), default=0)

    # ---- Gains --------------------------------------------------------------
    sum_h = sum(h)                       # H(e^j0) numerator == DC gain * Q15
    sum_abs_h = sum(abs(v) for v in h)   # L1 norm -> accumulator bound
    center_tap = h[31]
    max_tap = max(h)
    min_tap = min(h)
    max_tap_index = h.index(max_tap)
    min_tap_index = h.index(min_tap)

    dc_gain_linear = sum_h / Q15
    dc_gain_dB = to_db(dc_gain_linear)

    # Nyquist (f = fs/2) gain: H(e^{j*pi}) = sum_k (-1)^k h[k]
    nyquist_gain = sum(((-1) ** k) * h[k] for k in range(N))
    nyquist_gain_linear = nyquist_gain / Q15
    nyquist_gain_dB = to_db(nyquist_gain_linear)

    # ---- Group delay / linear phase ----------------------------------------
    # For a symmetric FIR, H(e^jw) = A(w) * exp(-j w (N-1)/2) with A(w) real.
    # The phase is exactly -w*(N-1)/2 (linear), group delay constant.
    group_delay_samples = (N - 1) / 2.0
    # Nominal audio sample rate for an absolute-time reading.
    fs = 16000.0

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""CSAW 2026 Challenge 3 -- Phase 05 DSP characterization.

FACET: coeffs-impulse
Load the recovered Q1.15 FIR taps and characterize the impulse response.

The impulse response of an FIR filter IS its coefficient set: h[n] = coeffs[n].
This script loads the golden taps, measures every structural/gain property the
facet calls for, writes impulse_response.csv, and emits coeffs-impulse.json.

Run:
  python C:/Users/lowbr/Documents/College/AI/CSAW_FIN_worktrees/05d-opus-dsp/experiments/phase05/05d-opus-dsp/ai/analysis/coeffs-impulse.py

All inputs are read from the read-only golden/ artifacts; nothing is modified.
"""
import json
import math
import csv
import os
import sys
import importlib.util

# ---- Absolute paths (do not depend on cwd) ---------------------------------
ROOT = "C:/Users/lowbr/Documents/College/AI/CSAW_FIN_worktrees/05d-opus-dsp/experiments/phase05/05d-opus-dsp"
COEFFS_PATH = os.path.join(ROOT, "golden", "coeffs.json")
SW_FIR_PATH = os.path.join(ROOT, "golden", "sw_fir.py")
OUT_JSON = os.path.join(ROOT, "reports", "analysis", "coeffs-impulse.json")
OUT_CSV = os.path.join(ROOT, "reports", "analysis", "impulse_response.csv")

Q15 = 32768.0  # 2^15, the Q1.15 scale (coeff/Q15 == float gain)


def load_golden_coeffs():
    """Load taps directly from the golden JSON, and cross-check against the
    golden sw_fir.load_coeffs() loader so we are provably using the same data
    path the bit-exact software model uses."""
    with open(COEFFS_PATH) as f:
        meta = json.load(f)
    coeffs = meta["coeffs_q15"]

    # Cross-check via the golden loader (fidelity guarantee).
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("sw_fir_golden", SW_FIR_PATH)
    sw = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(sw)
    coeffs_via_loader = sw.load_coeffs(COEFFS_PATH)
    assert coeffs_via_loader == coeffs, "golden loader disagreement!"

    return coeffs, meta


def classify_linear_phase_type(h):
    """Type I/II/III/IV per the standard linear-phase FIR taxonomy.

    symmetry  x  N parity  -> type
    symmetric  + N odd       Type I
    symmetric  + N even      Type II
    antisym    + N odd       Type III
    antisym    + N even      Type IV
    """
    N = len(h)
    is_sym = all(h[k] == h[N - 1 - k] for k in range(N))
    is_antisym = all(h[k] == -h[N - 1 - k] for k in range(N))
    n_odd = (N % 2 == 1)
    if is_sym and n_odd:
        t = "Type I"
    elif is_sym and not n_odd:
        t = "Type II"
    elif is_antisym and n_odd:
        t = "Type III"
    elif is_antisym and not n_odd:
        t = "Type IV"
    else:
        t = "none (not linear phase)"
    return t, is_sym, is_antisym


def to_db(ratio):
    if ratio == 0:
        return float("-inf")
    return 20.0 * math.log10(abs(ratio))


def main():
    h, meta = load_golden_coeffs()
    N = len(h)

    # ---- Structural symmetry -----------------------------------------------
    ftype, is_symmetric, is_antisymmetric = classify_linear_phase_type(h)

    # Per-element symmetry defects (which taps, if any, break h[k]==h[N-1-k]).
    asymmetry_defects = [
        {"k": k, "h_k": h[k], "h_mirror": h[N - 1 - k], "diff": h[k] - h[N - 1 - k]}
        for k in range(N // 2)
        if h[k] != h[N - 1 - k]
    ]
    max_abs_asymmetry = max((abs(d["diff"]) for d in asymmetry_defects), default=0)

    # ---- Gains --------------------------------------------------------------
    sum_h = sum(h)                       # H(e^j0) numerator == DC gain * Q15
    sum_abs_h = sum(abs(v) for v in h)   # L1 norm -> accumulator bound
    center_tap = h[31]
    max_tap = max(h)
    min_tap = min(h)
    max_tap_index = h.index(max_tap)
    min_tap_index = h.index(min_tap)

    dc_gain_linear = sum_h / Q15
    dc_gain_dB = to_db(dc_gain_linear)

    # Nyquist (f = fs/2) gain: H(e^{j*pi}) = sum_k (-1)^k h[k]
    nyquist_gain = sum(((-1) ** k) * h[k] for k in range(N))
    nyquist_gain_linear = nyquist_gain / Q15
    nyquist_gain_dB = to_db(nyquist_gain_linear)

    # ---- Group delay / linear phase ----------------------------------------
    # For a symmetric FIR, H(e^jw) = A(w) * exp(-j w (N-1)/2) with A(w) real.
    # The phase is exactly -w*(N-1)/2 (linear), group delay constant.
    group_delay_samples = (N - 1) / 2.0
    # Nominal audio sample rate for an absolute-time reading.
    fs = 16000.0
    group_delay_seconds = group_delay_samples / fs

    # ---- Accumulator bound from L1 norm ------------------------------------
    # acc = sum_k h[k]*x[n-k]; |x| <= 32768 (int16 value -32768 has magnitude
    # 2^15). Worst-case |acc| = 32768 * sum_abs_h.
    max_input_magnitude = 32768
    max_abs_acc = max_input_magnitude * sum_abs_h
    # Signed two's-complement width that holds [-max_abs_acc, +max_abs_acc].
    acc_bits_signed = max_abs_acc.bit_length() + 1  # +1 sign bit

    # Center-tap dominance (trojan-relevant: how much of the DC gain is h[31]).
    center_tap_fraction_of_q15 = center_tap / Q15      # h[31]/32768
    center_tap_fraction_of_sum_h = center_tap / sum_h  # share of DC gain
    center_tap_fraction_of_sum_abs = center_tap / sum_abs_h

    # ---- impulse_response.csv ----------------------------------------------
    with open(OUT_CSV, "w", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.writer(f)
        w.writerow(["index", "h_q15", "h_float"])
        for n in range(N):
            w.writerow([n, h[n], f"{h[n] / Q15:.10f}"])

        import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 4))
        ax.stem(range(N), h)
        ax.axvline(group_delay_samples, color="r", ls="--", lw=0.8,
                   label=f"center / group delay = {group_delay_samples:g}")
        ax.set_title("Recovered 63-tap FIR impulse response (Q1.15)")
        ax.set_xlabel("tap index n")
        ax.set_ylabel("h[n] (Q1.15 int)")
        ax.legend()
        fig.tight_layout()
        plot_path = os.path.join(ROOT, "reports", "analysis", "impulse_response.png")
        fig.savefig(plot_path, dpi=110)
        plt.close(fig)
    except Exception as e:  # matplotlib missing or headless failure -> skip
        plot_path = None
        sys.stderr.write(f"[info] plot skipped: {e}\n")

    # ---- Results ------------------------------------------------------------
    results = {
        "facet": "coeffs-impulse",
        "source_coeffs": COEFFS_PATH,
        "N": N,
        "is_symmetric": is_symmetric,
        "is_antisymmetric": is_antisymmetric,
        "symmetry_defects": asymmetry_defects,
        "max_abs_asymmetry": max_abs_asymmetry,
        "sum_h": sum_h,
        "center_tap": center_tap,
        "max_tap": max_tap,
        "max_tap_index": max_tap_index,
        "min_tap": min_tap,
        "min_tap_index": min_tap_index,
        "sum_abs_h": sum_abs_h,
        "dc_gain_linear": dc_gain_linear,
        "dc_gain_dB": dc_gain_dB,
        "nyquist_gain": nyquist_gain,
        "nyquist_gain_linear": nyquist_gain_linear,
        "nyquist_gain_dB": nyquist_gain_dB,
        "group_delay_samples": group_delay_samples,
        "group_delay_seconds_at_fs16000": group_delay_seconds,
        "fs_hz": fs,
        "filter_type": ftype,
        "linear_phase": is_symmetric or is_antisymmetric,
        "max_input_magnitude": max_input_magnitude,
        "max_abs_acc": max_abs_acc,
        "acc_bits_signed": acc_bits_signed,
        "center_tap_fraction_of_q15": center_tap_fraction_of_q15,
        "center_tap_fraction_of_sum_h": center_tap_fraction_of_sum_h,
        "center_tap_fraction_of_sum_abs_h": center_tap_fraction_of_sum_abs,
        "golden_meta": {
            "symmetric": meta.get("symmetric"),
            "sum_q15": meta.get("sum_q15"),
            "LAT": meta.get("LAT"),
            "msb_first": meta.get("msb_first"),
            "boff": meta.get("boff"),
        },
        "outputs": {
            "impulse_response_csv": OUT_CSV,
            "impulse_response_png": plot_path,
        },
        "notes": {
            "impulse_response": "For an FIR, the impulse response equals the "
                "coefficient vector h[n]; impulse_response.csv lists it directly.",
            "linear_phase_proof": "h symmetric (h[k]=h[N-1-k]) => "
                "H(e^jw)=A(w)*exp(-j w (N-1)/2) with A(w) real, so phase = "
                "-w*(N-1)/2 is exactly linear and group delay = (N-1)/2 is "
                "constant at all frequencies.",
            "accumulator_bound": "|acc| <= 32768 * sum_abs_h; a signed "
                f"{acc_bits_signed}-bit accumulator holds the worst case with "
                "no overflow.",
        },
    }

    with open(OUT_JSON, "w") as f:
        json.dump(results, f, indent=2)

    # ---- Console summary ----------------------------------------------------
    print("=== coeffs-impulse ===")

content.text: All outputs verified. The JSON holds every measurement, the CSV has 64 lines (header + 63 taps), and symmetry is visible in the head/tail (h[0]=h[62]=-14, h[1]=h[61]=20, etc.). The script also cross-checked the taps against the golden `sw_fir.load_coeffs()` loader (the assert passed). Returning the structured result.

key_findings: Recovered filter is a 63-tap Type I linear-phase FIR low-pass: symmetric (h[k]==h[N-1-k] for all k, zero asymmetry defects) with odd length N=63 (even order 62).

Exact linear phase: symmetry gives H(e^jw)=A(w)*exp(-j*w*31) with A(w) real, so phase is exactly -w*31 and group delay is constant = (N-1)/2 = 31 samples = 1.9375 ms at fs=16000 Hz (this is the intrinsic filter delay, separate from the 2-frame I2S framing latency).
Unity DC/passband gain: sum_h = 32768 = exactly 1.0 in Q1.15 => dc_gain_dB = 0.000 dB; this matches the golden meta sum_q15=32768.
Strong low-pass behavior at Nyquist: nyquist_gain = sum_k (-1)^k h[k] = -28, i.e. -0.000854 linear = -61.37 dB at fs/2 = 8000 Hz (small nonzero residual, not a true null).
Center tap h[31]=13920 is the global maximum and dominates: it alone is 42.48% of sum_h (h[31]/32768 = 0.4248). Largest negative tap is -2587 at index 28.
L1 norm sum_abs_h = 63248 bounds the accumulator: worst-case |acc| = 32768 * 63248 = 2,072,510,464 < 2^31, so a signed 32-bit accumulator holds it with no overflow.
Impulse response equals the coefficient vector; written to impulse_response.csv (63 rows, index/h_q15/h_float), symmetry confirmed by head/tail (h[0]=h[62]=-14, h[1]=h[61]=20).
trojan_implications: Center-tap dominance is the highest-leverage payload lever: h[31] carries 42.48% of the DC/passband gain (h[31]/32768=0.4248), so a trigger that nudges the center tap moves gain/DC the most per unit coefficient delta -- efficient but also the most conspicuous to a magnitude check. Outer taps contribute little individually, so tampering them is stealthier but needs larger deltas to produce a measurable payload.

Breaking symmetry (h[k] != h[N-1-k]) destroys the exact linear phase: group delay stops being the flat 31 samples and becomes frequency-dependent (group-delay ripple / phase distortion) even when the magnitude response is barely changed. A phase or group-delay probe is therefore a sensitive detector of any asymmetric-tap trojan, and the untriggered golden path must keep its constant 31-sample group delay to remain bit-identical.

Accumulator headroom bounds any magnitude payload: worst-case |acc| = 32768*sum_abs_h = 2,072,510,464 sits just under 2^31 (2,147,483,648), leaving only ~74.97M LSB (~3.5% of signed-32-bit full scale) of slack before the (acc+2^14)>>15 then int16-saturate stage clips. A payload that injects extra weighted energy on a trigger has only that margin before producing obvious saturation artifacts.

DC/passband gain is pinned to exactly 1.0 (sum_h=32768); the golden untriggered output must preserve sum_h exactly to stay bit-identical, so a payload may only diverge in the triggered state. A trivial static detector is sum_h != 32768 (or loss of perfect tap symmetry), meaning a stealthy Trojan should hide in trigger-gated logic rather than in altered static coefficients.
uncertainties: matplotlib is not installed in this environment, so the optional impulse_response.png stem plot was skipped (impulse_response.png not written); all CSV/JSON numeric outputs were written as required and do not depend on plotting.
nyquist_gain is a small nonzero residual (-28, i.e. -61.37 dB), not an exact zero, so attenuation at fs/2 is finite rather than a perfect null -- expected for a finite-length windowed low-pass.
Hz interpretations (group delay 1.9375 ms, Nyquist at 8000 Hz) assume the nominal fs=16000 Hz given in the task; the tap values themselves are sample-rate-independent.
